name: Blackcurrant
grown_as: A fruit bush, 'Ben Conan', a compact Scottish variety with large berries. Grown as a stool: many stems from below the soil, no trunk.
habit: A bushy, upright, spineless deciduous shrub, 1 to 1.5 m high and wide, with many stems rising from the base. The whole plant has a strong, sharp blackcurrant smell when touched, from tiny resin glands.

leaf.outline: About as wide as long, 5 to 10 cm, with three main lobes and often two small extra lobes at the base
leaf.tip: Each lobe broadly triangular and pointed; the middle lobe largest
leaf.margin: Coarse, irregular, fairly sharp teeth (often double) all round every lobe
leaf.veins: Three to five main veins from the top of the stalk, one into each lobe, pressed in so the leaf looks a little puckered
leaf.surface: Dull green and smooth above; paler and a little downy beneath, dotted with tiny yellow resin glands
leaf.stalk: Long, 3 to 6 cm, downy, widening where it clasps the stem

flower.form: A small bell, open at the mouth
flower.petals: Five tiny whitish petals inside the bell, hardly seen; the bell itself is made of five sepals joined at the base, their tips curling back
flower.colour: Dull greenish-cream inside, flushed pinkish-purple and downy outside
flower.centre: Five short stamens and a style inside the bell
flower.behind: The swollen green ovary just above the bell, which becomes the berry
flower.carried: Five to ten on a hanging string (strig) 3 to 7 cm long, from the older wood where the leaves join it

fruit: Round berries, 1 to 1.5 cm, glossy black when ripe (green, then reddish, then black), each with a dry brown tuft of old flower at its tip. Five to ten on a hanging strig, ripening together; 'Ben Conan' has large berries on short strigs. July.
seedling: Not drawn: grown from cuttings or bought plants
winter: Bare, upright pale brown to grey stems from the base, young ones paler tan; fat, pointed, pale buds with loose scales (swollen round ones are big bud mite).

leaf: three main pointed lobes, often two small ones at the base
heart-shaped base on a long stalk
coarse irregular teeth all round every lobe
main veins fanning from the stalk
bloom: a small bell-shaped flower with tips curling back, pinkish outside and greenish-cream within
part of a hanging string of several flowers
young: several upright stems from the soil, no trunk
dormant: bare upright stems from the base, no trunk
flower: short hanging strings of small bell flowers
young three-lobed leaves just opening around them
crop: hanging strings of glossy round black berries

look_alikes: Redcurrant and whitecurrant have smaller, less pointed leaves without the smell or glands, flat saucer flowers and longer strigs. Flowering currant (Ribes sanguineum) has bright pink flowers and bloomy blue-black berries. Jostaberry (a cross with gooseberry) is larger and less smelly, with glossier leaves.
